chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Malik al-Hadrami, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) — in a long hadith — in which he says:

Verily, when God, the Blessed and Exalted, made His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ascend [on the Night Journey], He said to him: O Muhammad! Your prophethood has been completed and your sustenance has been cut off, so who will be for your community after you? So I said: O Lord! I have examined Your creation, but I did not find anyone more obedient to me than Ali ibn Abi Talib. So He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: Me too, O Muhammad, so who is for your community? I said: O Lord! I have examined Your creation, but I did not find anyone with a more intense love for me than Ali ibn Abi Talib. So He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: Me too, O Muhammad, so inform him that he is the Banner of Guidance, the Imam of My devotees, and a light for whoever obeys Me.

key_terms.أَكْل: Literally 'eating/food'; here refers metaphorically to the Prophet's worldly sustenance and life coming to an end
key_terms.إِمَامُ أَوْلِيَائِي: Imam of My devotees/friends — referring to those who have attained spiritual closeness to God
key_terms.رَايَةُ الْهُدَى: Banner of Guidance — a title affirming Ali's role as the guide and leader
key_terms.نُبُوَّةٌ: Prophethood — the divinely entrusted mission of the Prophet which concluded with his death

ai.seo_question: What did God say to the Prophet during the Night Journey about Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: This excerpt from a longer hadith of Imam al-Baqir (AS) describes a divine conversation during the Prophet's Night Journey (Isra). God informs the Prophet that his prophethood has reached completion and asks who shall lead the Muslim community after him. The Prophet twice testifies to Ali ibn Abi Talib's unparalleled obedience and love, and God confirms these qualities and commands the Prophet to convey Ali's three-fold spiritual status: Banner of Guidance, Imam of the Awliya', and a Light for believers. This hadith was understood by early Shia audiences as a divine designation (nass) of the Imamate of Ali.
